summary: connector state drift causes tenant to serve mixed model versions after aborted rollout
description: Issue summary: During an aborted canary promotion for Translingo's dedicated cluster, a subset of tenant sessions continued routing to the pre-promote model while others followed the new model leading to inconsistent outputs. Impact: customer reports production traffic returning inconsistent translations for the same request signature; affects downstream QA and live traffic. Background: Customer was performing a staged promote from openlm-13b-v2 -> rw-compat-7b with a canary weight increase at 09:00 UTC and an abort at 09:17 UTC when latency spike was observed. Expected: abort should preserve the pinned model for in-flight sessions and roll back canary state globally. Observed: ~12% of sessions observed responses from rw-compat-7b after abort; other sessions continued on openlm-13b-v2.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Customer starts canary promote on dedicated pool with 5% -> 25% weight steps.
2) At weight 25% monitor latency graphs for tenant-translingo cluster.
3) Abort rollout using console 'Abort Promote' at 09:17 UTC.
4) Send identical inference requests (same session tokens) to endpoint and compare model outputs across repeated requests.
5) Observe that subset of session tokens continue to be routed to promoted model while others route back to original model.

[09:12:03] router: allocate session token s:abcd1234 -> backend rw-compat-7b (canary)
[09:16:58] metrics: tenant=translingo latency_p95 spike -> 820ms
[09:17:10] console: user Leah P pressed 'Abort Promote' -> promote aborted
[09:17:12] router: canary weight set -> 0% but connector-state sync pending for shard-7
[09:18:01] session-store: sticky-token s:abcd1234 last-bound=rw-compat-7b ttl=2h
[09:19:05] inference: request s:abcd1234 returned model=rw-compat-7b
[09:20:22] router: sync completed for shards 1-6; shard-7 backlog processed 09:20:10-09:20:20
[09:20:26] inference: request s:efgh5678 returned model=openlm-13b-v2
investigation_notes: Timeline and initial findings: Support verified abort event in console at 09:17 UTC and canary weight drop at control plane. Router logs show immediate weight change but connector-state sync to all edge shards completed only at 09:20:10; shard-7 processed backlog later which left sticky bindings for sessions created during canary. Hypothesis: session-store sticky bindings (connector-level cache) were not invalidated on abort for in-flight sessions on certain edge shards, leading to divergent session affinity. We reproduced locally on a staging mimic by creating sticky tokens and aborting promote: observed identical behavior when connector sync lag > 90s. Related signals: session-store TTLs set to 2 hours; sticky-token TTL prevented immediate unbind. Partial fix applied: forced session-store unbind for tenant translingo on shard-7, observed routing normalize to openlm-13b-v2 for subsequent requests. Further steps: implement explicit 'unbind-on-abort' control-plane action that issues invalidate-sticky API to session-store for affected shards; add health-check to detect sync backlog > 30s and surface console warning. Dashboards reviewed: https://internal.grafana.company/r/rollouts?orgId=1&var-tenant=translingo (console link). Related previous tickets: SUP-31147 (session-resume-drops-version-affinity-causes-fallback) similar pattern but not identical.

2024-11-03 09:22 UTC - Eng (Serving Runtime): Investigating why connector sync lag occurred: preliminary suspected cause was a GC spike on shard-7 edge agent between 09:15-09:18 that delayed processing of control-plane messages.
2024-11-04 14:00 UTC - Product: Proposed console change: show 'pending-sync' warning and add a one-click 'Invalidate sticky bindings for tenant' during abort flows.
resolution_notes: Workaround: manually invalidated sticky bindings for affected shards which restored consistent routing for translingo sessions. Permanent fix timeline: engineering will land a control-plane change to call session-store invalidate for in-flight sessions on aborts (PR linked). Additional mitigation: add connectivity/queue depth alerting on edge agents to prevent >30s control-plane processing delays. Follow-up: schedule patch release to staging 2024-11-10 and prod 2024-11-15 after QA. Customer follow-up: Translingo to run verification test plan post-release and confirm closure.
